I have a microservices application with 15 services. Each service has its own database. Users are complaining about slow response times during peak hours. The p99 latency is 4 seconds. Our infrastructure runs on Kubernetes with 3 nodes. We use Redis for caching but the cache hit rate is only 20%. Network calls between services average 50ms each and a typical user request triggers 8 downstream service calls. Please analyze this situation and provide a detailed remediation plan covering caching strategy, service mesh configuration, database query optimization, and horizontal scaling recommendations.

Our e-commerce platform processes 50,000 orders per day. We recently migrated from a monolith to microservices. Since the migration, we are seeing data inconsistency issues where an order shows as confirmed in the orders service but payment has not been processed in the payments service. We need a solution that guarantees exactly-once processing, handles partial failures gracefully, and maintains an audit trail. The system needs to handle up to 200 transactions per second with sub-100ms latency. Please provide a comprehensive architecture recommendation including the saga pattern, event sourcing, CQRS, and distributed transaction management with concrete implementation steps.

We are building a machine learning pipeline that needs to process 10TB of training data daily. The data comes from 50 different sources in varying formats including JSON, CSV, Parquet, and raw text. We need feature engineering, data validation, model training, and real-time inference serving. The team has experience with Python but limited experience with distributed systems. Our budget is constrained and we want to avoid vendor lock-in. Please provide a detailed end-to-end architecture recommendation covering data ingestion, storage, processing, model versioning, and deployment strategy with trade-offs for each major decision point.

I am designing a real-time collaborative document editor similar to Google Docs. The system needs to support up to 100 simultaneous editors on a single document, handle network partitions gracefully, merge conflicting edits correctly, and maintain a full revision history. Latency for local edits must feel instantaneous while syncing with the server within 500ms. Offline editing must be supported with automatic conflict resolution when connectivity is restored. Please explain the operational transformation versus CRDT approaches, their trade-offs, and recommend a concrete implementation strategy with data structures and synchronization protocol details.

Our authentication system currently uses username and password with bcrypt hashing. We want to upgrade to a zero-trust security model. We have 2 million users and 500 enterprise clients who use SSO. We need to support FIDO2 passkeys, TOTP, and SMS OTP as second factors. The system must be GDPR compliant, support account recovery without weakening security, handle bot attacks and credential stuffing, and provide detailed audit logs for compliance. Please design a comprehensive authentication architecture covering token lifecycle management, session handling, multi-device support, and migration strategy for existing users.

We run a SaaS product used by 800 enterprise customers. Each customer has between 10 and 50,000 users. We are experiencing multi-tenancy isolation issues where one large tenant's heavy queries are affecting other tenants' performance. We currently use a shared database with tenant_id columns. Our largest tenant generates 40% of all database load. Please analyze the trade-offs between shared schema, schema-per-tenant, and database-per-tenant approaches, provide migration strategies for each, explain how to implement query quotas and rate limiting at the database level, and recommend a path forward that balances cost efficiency with performance isolation.
